title: Other sources of income
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-ways-earn-income, covers wages, profit, dividends, rent and government payments but not interest on savings, which the new point includes, so it teaches a narrower set of sources and would need a new element rather than small changes.

draft.title: Other sources of income
card: Income is money received. Many Australians earn it from work, but it can come from other sources too.
money left for the owner of a business after all its costs are paid.
money a bank pays you for keeping your savings with it. Dividends are a share of a company's profit, paid to people who own shares in it.
money a property owner receives from a tenant who uses the property. Government payments, such as Youth Allowance, are money the government pays to people who meet set rules.
draft.remember: Income can come from a business, savings, shares, property or the government, as well as from work.

a.q: Jai owns shares in a company. The company pays him part of its profit each year. What is this income called?
a.why: A dividend is a share of a company's profit paid to the people who own shares. Interest is tempting, but it is paid by a bank on savings, not by a company to its owners.
a.clue: Jai owns part of the company.

b.q: Priya has $2000 in a bank account. Each year the bank adds some money to the account. What type of income is this?
b.why: The bank pays interest to people for keeping their savings with it. A dividend is tempting because it is also money from owning something, but dividends come from company shares, not from a bank account.
b.clue: Think about who is paying the money and what it is for.
